subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Grace Li <grace@brightlearn.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up

Hi Grace - thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

Summary of needs (from the call):
- You want an eval to validate model fit for structured output (JSON) for BrightLearn's course ingestion pipeline.
- Key checks: JSON schema compliance, robust retries/partial failures for tool-calling, extraction accuracy on edge cases (nested lists, missing fields), and P95 latency for 75-150 token outputs.
- You also asked for benchmark links, recommended models, and a suggested eval plan.

What we recommend (short):
- Model: redwood-instruct-4x (primary) - best balance of structured-output fidelity and quality.
- Fallback: redwood-chat-3.2 (lower latency, slightly looser on strict schema enforcement).
- Eval focus: schema validation (AJV), function-calling retries (exponential backoff, idempotency keys), generation determinism for core fields, and regression checks against your golden set.

Attached: model_benchmarks_2026-07.pdf (latency/cost/quality across candidates), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (initial prompts + expected JSON), mutual_action_plan_brightlearn.xlsx (timeline & owners).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a redacted sample of ~500 records (JSON) + target JSON Schema and any must-have fields by EOD Tue (7/13).
2) We run a 2-stage eval: a small proof (500 records) to validate schema compliance + a broader run (10k) for regression and latency profiling.
3) Tech sync with Dev (30-45m) to confirm edge cases and integration points (webhooks, retries) - proposed week of 7/20.

What we'll report back: per-field precision/recall, percent of outputs that validate against schema (AJV pass rate), examples of schema failures with original prompts, P50/P95 latency and token-cost estimate, and recommended model/quantization profile.

Questions for you:
- Can BrightLearn share the JSON Schema and a redacted sample by 7/13?
- Are there regulatory constraints (PII handling, retention windows) we should include in the evaluation?

Happy to jump on a quick calendar invite if that helps.

-

Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A few quick clarifications:

1) Latency: our SLA target for production is P95 <= 400ms for the 75-token median output. Are the numbers in your benchmark PDF for hosted vs Dedicated? We're primarily interested in hosted API first.

2) Schema: we can share a redacted JSON Schema and 500 examples (will remove any direct PII). Is AJV the right validator for you? We use a slightly custom schema with optional nested arrays - want to ensure edge cases are covered.

3) Security/compliance: procurement needs a SOC 2 report and the security questionnaire - can you send the latest versions? Also curious about data retention on the hosted offering.

If you can include a rough cost per 1k tokens for the proposed models (hosted), that'd help our procurement team.

Happy to take the tech sync with Dev - Alix looped in for procurement.

-

Head of Integrations | BrightLearn Inc
+1 212-555-7788

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Grace Li <grace@brightlearn.com>

Date: 2026-07-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up

Thanks Grace - answers inline below.

Latency/cost: the attached model_benchmarks_2026-07.pdf includes hosted (multi-tenant) and Dedicated numbers. Short ballpark (hosted API):
- redwood-instruct-4x: P50 ~ 120-180ms (75 tokens), P95 ~ 320-420ms (depends on region and load).
- redwood-chat-3.2: P50 ~ 80-120ms, P95 ~ 240-310ms.
Cost estimate (hosted, ballpark):
- redwood-instruct-4x: ~$0.12 per 1k prompt tokens / $0.20 per 1k completion tokens (varies by commit).
- redwood-chat-3.2: ~30-40% lower cost.

Schema & validator: AJV is fine - our eval harness uses AJV for schema validation and will also log full parse traces for any failure so we can root-cause (prompt vs model). Please include examples of the nested-array edge cases.

Security docs: Neha (cc'd) will send SOC 2 and the security questionnaire + answers. For hosted: default retention is 30 days for request metadata, no user content stored beyond that unless you opt into retention for fine-tuning. We'll confirm specifics in the security packet.

Eval plan & timeline: we can start the small 500-record run as soon as you share the redacted set. After that, we'll propose a 10k run to measure regressions and P95 under realistic batching. Expected delivery for the 500-record pass: 3 business days from receipt.

Next steps I'll take this week:
- Send SOC 2 + security packet (Neha).
- Share a short tech-runbook for the eval harness (Dev) and a link to the test plan: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/model-fit-2026#test-plan
- Lock a 30-45m tech sync for the week of 7/20 - Dev will propose times.

If that all sounds good I'll mark the MAP and calendar items and we'll start.

-

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Grace Li <grace@brightlearn.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up

Hi Grace - quick note from the engineering side on the eval harness and how we'll validate structured output.

Eval harness highlights:
- Schema validation: we run AJV (v8) against each output; failures are bucketed by error type (missing required, type mismatch, additionalProperties, etc.).
- Retries & idempotency: for function-calling paths we'll simulate transient failures and exercise up to 3 retries with exponential backoff (200ms -> 500ms -> 1s). Each request includes an idempotency key so duplicate tool actions can be detected.
- Edge cases: please include prompts that exercise nested arrays, optional keys, and fields with mixed numeric/string typing. We'll fuzz 10% of the sample set with malformed inputs to measure recovery.
- Logging/artifacts: we'll provide a CSV of per-record results, raw model outputs, and a small set of failing examples annotated with the AJV trace.

Can you upload the schema + redacted samples to the Drive link Marissa shared (or send via secure transfer)? Once we have them I'll kick off the 500-record run and share results within ~72 hours.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
